paraphrase: Something in this world is being moved (reduced from potency to act in some respect); this is evident to the senses.

self_evident.note: Floor item F4 (#1007), approved by the owner on the observation basis. Aquinas takes it as evident to the senses (sensu constat), not demonstrated. Its two recorded rivals stay recorded and unrefuted: the Eleatic thesis that nothing is moved (Melissus as Aristotle reports him) and the McTaggart-style thesis that nothing is moved though there are judgings. So the observation criterion is not mechanically met (its sceptical rivals are not refuted), and the premise is established relative to the owner's approval, not by a refutation of those rivals.
